changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For finance buyers at domestic B2B sellers and invoice-driven businesses (distributors), open with M9 in their words instead of the global-infrastructure line: 'Know where every deposit came from, and close month-end without a week of archaeology.' Avoid 'infrastructure' and 'payments'; say 'deposits' and 'month-end'. Follow straight into the payout-to-transaction-to-ERP demo.
changes.why: The M1 opener met 'Silence', the buyer never said 'payments' or 'infrastructure' and talked about 'the deposits' and 'I just want to know where my money is', so an opener built on her words and the reconciliation outcome fits her better than ours.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For CFOs and finance buyers, lead the value proof with a reconciliation cost workup built from one month of the customer's own statements (manual matching hours plus unmatched-deposit write-offs), offered right after the reconciliation demo: 'Send us one month of statements and we'll price what month-end costs you today.' Keep the independent study as backup, not the main proof.
changes.why: The deal went from 'I had it at 20 percent' to signed after the rep priced the CFO's pain from her own statements, which she valued because 'that's my number, not yours.'

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: Stop leading with the developer story when the economic buyer is in finance. Keep APIs, docs and sandbox in a technical appendix for the IT contact, and put the close or reconciliation outcome in finance terms on page one of any proposal that may reach a CFO.
changes.why: The developer story 'went nowhere', and the first proposal, written around portal, checkout and APIs, was rejected on page one by the CFO who decided the deal.

changes.change: Add a distributor or wholesale customer story with a reference call that finance buyers can take. Use it in place of retail and software stories when selling to distributors and wholesalers.
changes.why: Our existing customer stories were dismissed with 'this is a company that sells sweaters', and the buyer raised the missing distributor reference twice even though she signed.
